Extract information about a constructed heatmap

Source: R/heat_map-internals.R
heat_map_info.Rd

heat_map_info() returns the data and layout used to construct a heatmap, including the order of rows and columns, cluster assignments and dendrograms, so that they can be used in downstream analyses.

Usage

heat_map_info(x)

Arguments

x

object of class heat_map returned by heat_map.

Value

a list containing:

  • data: the data displayed in the heatmap (after scaling).

  • row_order: indices of the rows of x in the order they are displayed from the top to the bottom of the heatmap.

  • col_order: indices of the columns of x in the order they are displayed from left to right.

  • row_clusters, col_clusters: the cluster assigned to each row/column in their original order (or NULL when no clusters were defined). Clusters are numbered in the order they are displayed: from left to right for columns and from top to bottom for rows.

  • tree_x, tree_y: hclust objects for the x and y axis dendrograms (or NULL). Branch heights are rescaled for display.

  • support_x, support_y: bootstrap support of each merge of tree_x and tree_y (tree_support_x, tree_support_y), NA for the root and merges fixed by groups, or NULL.

  • zoom_x, zoom_y: indices of the columns (from left to right) and rows (from top to bottom) enlarged in a zoom panel (zoom_x, zoom_y) - a list with the indices of each band when several were given as a list - or NULL.

  • axis_text_x, axis_text_y: axis labels from left to right and from top to bottom respectively.

  • colours, sizes, shapes: the fill colour, relative size and shape of each cell, in the orientation of the original data.

  • centers: lists x and y with the centre of each column and row in the original order, in the heatmap's plot co-ordinates (one unit per cell, plus any gaps between clusters), for drawing on top of a heatmap.

  • split_colours, split_data: the fill colour and value (after scaling) of the lower right half of each cell (cell_split) in the orientation of the original data, or NULL.

  • annotations: lists x and y with the colour of each row/column for every annotation, in the original order.

  • layout: a data.frame with the bounding box (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) of each component of the heatmap in inches from the bottom left corner of the device.

  • raster: whether the cells were drawn as raster images (see cell_raster in heat_map()).

  • col_limits, size_limits: limits of the colour and size scales.

Author

Dillon Hammill (dillon.hammill21@gmail.com)

Examples

hm <- heat_map(
  mtcars,
  scale = "column",
  tree_cut_x = 3,
  tree_cut_y = 4,
  popup = FALSE
)
#> Applying range scaling to each column...

info <- heat_map_info(hm)
info$col_clusters
#>  mpg  cyl disp   hp drat   wt qsec   vs   am gear carb 
#>    3    1    1    1    3    1    3    3    2    2    1 
rownames(mtcars)[info$row_order]
#>  [1] "Ford Pantera L"      "Maserati Bora"       "Chrysler Imperial"  
#>  [4] "Cadillac Fleetwood"  "Lincoln Continental" "Duster 360"         
#>  [7] "Camaro Z28"          "Hornet Sportabout"   "Pontiac Firebird"   
#> [10] "Merc 450SLC"         "Merc 450SE"          "Merc 450SL"         
#> [13] "Dodge Challenger"    "AMC Javelin"         "Toyota Corona"      
#> [16] "Merc 240D"           "Merc 230"            "Merc 280"           
#> [19] "Merc 280C"           "Hornet 4 Drive"      "Valiant"            
#> [22] "Lotus Europa"        "Datsun 710"          "Volvo 142E"         
#> [25] "Honda Civic"         "Fiat X1-9"           "Fiat 128"
